title: Strictly positive integral grading of a sharp lattice monoid
statement: Let $G$ be a free abelian group of finite rank (a free $\mathbf Z$-module with finite basis [def-weil-pbc-free-module]), meaning a group isomorphic to $\mathbf Z^r$ for some integer $r\ge0$. Let $P\subseteq G$ be an additive submonoid generated by a finite set, and assume $P\cap(-P)=\{0\}$. Then there is a group homomorphism $w:G\to\mathbf Z$ such that $w(p)>0$ for every $p\in P\setminus\{0\}$. Its restriction is an additive map $P\to\mathbf N$. The trivial monoid $P=\{0\}$ is allowed.

source.place: Agent-supplied convex-algebra refinement for the sharp fs monoids of VI 1.6, printed p. 70, and VIII 3.1.1, 3.1.10, printed pp. 98--99. Strict positivity is a rational cone separation input, not a theorem asserted verbatim in ILO.

proof.text: Choose a finite generating set s for P and enumerate it by Fin |s|. Use the given integral basis to embed G injectively in V = (Fin r → ℚ) by integer coordinates. Prove that any rational cone element x has a positive natural multiple d x equal to the image of an element of P: clear the finite coefficient denominators, whose nonnegative integer numerators give a natural linear combination of the generators. A private finite-set induction clears denominators, also for empty families.

source.place: Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103; denominator-clearing and sharpness argument supplied here.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-rational-cone-dual-finite] to the images of the generators and sum the resulting forms to obtain L. Every p in P has a natural generator expansion, so all forms are nonnegative at its image. If L vanishes there, every individual form vanishes; thus the negative of the image also belongs to the cone. Step 1 gives a positive d and a in P with image(a) = -d image(p). Injectivity gives a = -d p. Sharpness applied to d p forces d p = 0; its image in a rational vector space and positivity of d force p = 0. Consequently L is strictly positive on all nonzero elements of P. Empty generator or form families are covered by the same finite-sum reasoning.

source.place: Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103 is motivating context only. The finite rational half-space description is the cited DAG statement (its Kato 1994 source remains WANTED); summing the defining forms and using pointedness is the elementary agent-supplied argument written here.

proof.text: Apply the finite common-denominator lemma to the values of L on the standard coordinate vectors of V, obtaining d > 0 and integers z_i = d L(e_i). Define w(g) = ∑_i coordinate_i(g) z_i. This is explicitly an additive integer-valued map. Expanding the rational coordinate vector of g in the standard coordinate vectors proves w(g) = d L(image(g)) after rational casting. Positivity from Step 2 then gives strict positivity of w on nonzero P.

source.place: Agent-supplied lattice-coordinate denominator-clearing argument following Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103.

proof.text: For p in P, split into p = 0 and p ≠ 0 to show w(p) ≥ 0. Define wP(p) = Int.toNat(w(p)). Nonnegativity proves the required integer-cast equality. Integer-cast injectivity and additivity of w prove additivity of wP. The zero monoid and rank-zero cases require no separate construction.

source.place: Agent-supplied final restriction argument; Expose VIII, Remark 3.1.29, printed p. 103.

proof_origin.place: B5 Lean proof follows the finite rational half-space route, using integral basis coordinates, finite-set denominator clearing, sharpness on a positive multiple of p when the sum of forms vanishes, and an explicit coordinate formula for the integer grading. The ILO remark remains motivating context only.
